correctness.rationale: Direct digit evaluation gives E_b(a sum_{i in I}b^i)=|I|a^3. A strict b^3 bound eliminates all positions >=3; the five remaining patterns are exhaustive. Each pattern gives one exact identity and conversely a valid base-b fixed point. The generalized Pell -3 family has an explicit positive inverse descent to (3,1), while the other two families are standard Pell. Counting the square and 2a^2-1 families with an O(log X) Pell overlap gives the asserted sharp asymptotics. An independent digit parser verified all bases 2 through 1000. Finite checks support but do not prove unbounded claims.

value.rationale: The object is the natural uniform-digit fixed-point subfamily of a recently introduced digit dynamical system. A complete all-base theorem, rather than a chosen small numerical range, identifies five and only five patterns, including three different infinite Pell mechanisms. The exact square-root counting law quantifies the frequency of bases admitting these special attractors and gives infinite nonsquare even-base obstructions relevant to an explicit open question. Classical Pell identities are tools rather than the claimed novelty.
